title: Monopoly & Imperfect Competition (HL) Adventure 1: Monopoly Inefficiency
welcome_lead: Today you'll see why monopolies produce too little, charge too much and waste welfare.
meta_desc: Economics HL: monopoly profit maximisation, allocative inefficiency, deadweight loss.
final_note: You derived monopoly output and the deadweight loss compared with perfect competition.

concepts.def: Single seller, high barriers to entry
Cost slack from lack of competition

walkthroughs.body_html:
A monopoly is a price-maker.

Because demand slopes down, selling one more unit reduces price on all units: MR < P.

Profit max at MR = MC. The monopolist then reads price off demand at that quantity.

Monopoly Qm < perfect competition Qpc. Price Pm > Ppc.

The triangle between demand and MC from Qm to Qpc is the deadweight loss.

Other costs: X-inefficiency (slack management), restricted choice, rent-seeking. Possible benefits: dynamic efficiency from R&D, economies of scale.

Where LRAC keeps falling over the whole market (utilities, rail), one large firm is cheapest overall.

Policy options: state ownership, price-cap regulation (RPI−X, UK), franchising.
